translations.answer: PRIME can refine robot logs into more contact-consistent trajectories, forces, and inertial parameters offline, but its runtime, use of future data, and unresolved identifiability prevent treating it as a real-time safety estimator or an unvalidated model update.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Kinematic measurements, torque estimates, and a contact-geometry model are time-aligned.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Identified parameters are cross-validated on held-out motions.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Offline Go2 and G1 robot logs.
translations.confidence_rationale: Force-plate comparison, identification ablations, and the official differentiable implementation support offline physical refinement; observability and full inertia ground truth remain open.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Equations 15–20 and 33–34, Tables I–III and VI, and Figures 3–12.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines differentiable contact and validates force and parameter refinement with documented runtime.
translations.evidence.0.title: PRIME: Physically-consistent Robotic Inertial and Motion Estimation for Legged and Humanoid Robots
translations.title: Can contact forces and inertial parameters recovered by PRIME be used directly in a real-time WBC?
